extracted.intended_audience: travel journalists, magazine editors, and freelance travel writers pitching or commissioning travel stories
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for selecting, pitching, and judging travel journalism stories for magazines/outlets, combining journalism standards with literary and service elements. Covers required story elements, newsworthiness drivers, story types, ethics, and implicit quality markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong scenes — vivid place description
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Story Elements (Required). Emphasises sensory, place-based description as a foundational element of travel writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nut graph — why this story now
rubrics_metrics.description: Nut graph — why this story now
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required element: a clear nut graph explaining timeliness and relevance (the 'why now') of the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid interviewees — locals, experts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required element: use credible interviewees (local people, subject-matter experts) to anchor reporting and provide authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data — historical, statistical context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required element: include relevant data or context (historical facts, statistics) to situate the story beyond personal anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'Top 10' listicle approach / seek unique narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: "Great travel journalism isn't about ticking off famous landmarks"; editors want stories "no one else is telling"; unique narratives only the writer can tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: listicles and obvious 'top 10' pieces. Preference for distinctive, original angles and narratives that differentiate the piece from ubiquitous list-style content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destination news
rubrics_metrics.description: Destination news — political change, opening, restriction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: developments at the destination (e.g., political events, openings or restrictions) that make travel-relevant reporting timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anniversary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: anniversaries or milestones that provide a hook for retrospective or contextual travel pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: festivals, cultural openings, or notable events that draw interest and structure a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Trends — types of travel (sustainable, slow, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: broader travel trends (e.g., sustainable travel, slow travel) that indicate a pattern worth reporting on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden gems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: spotlighting lesser-known places or experiences that offer novelty to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical changes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: concrete changes affecting travel logistics (visa rules, currency shifts, transit changes) offering utility to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate / environmental changes affecting travel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: environmental developments that alter travel patterns, accessibility, or safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hotel / restaurant openings (high-end)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: significant hospitality openings—particularly higher-end—that attract attention and signal new travel opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author's intimate experience — narrative voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness/angle driver: a compelling first-person perspective or intimate experience that provides unique narrative authority and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity / intersectional angle — who travels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness driver: stories that foreground identity (race, gender, disability, sexuality) and intersectional perspectives on travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destination novelty to audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: the destination should feel new or fresh to the outlet's audience, offering discovery or surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural depth — beyond surface
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: coverage should probe cultural context and depth rather than only surface-level observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility for would-be travelers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: include usable information — what to do, when to go, approximate costs — that helps readers plan travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspirational quality — luxury, exoticism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: pieces that inspire or offer aspirational appeal (luxury experiences, exotic locales) can be desirable depending on outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: the story should lend itself to strong photographic accompaniment; visual potential is valuable to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique angle — author's distinctive POV
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: a distinctive point of view from the author that differentiates the piece from other coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local voice prominence — not just Western tourist's view
rubrics_metrics.description: Local voice prominence — not just Western tourist's view
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: centre local perspectives to avoid a purely outsider or Western-centric narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability angle (rising)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: sustainable travel concerns are increasingly relevant and can strengthen a story's timeliness and ethical framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity intersection — race, gender, ability, sexuality of traveler
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity intersection — race, gender, ability, sexuality of traveler
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: foregrounding how identity shapes travel experiences can provide fresh, important perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service elements — what to do, when to go, how much
rubrics_metrics.description: Service elements — what to do, when to go, how much
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: even literary pieces often include service information that helps readers act on the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service piece — 'How to' / utility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story type: practical, how-to guides focused on utility and actionable advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destination feature — comprehensive place coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story type: an in-depth portrait of a place covering history, culture, logistics, and highlights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travelogue — first-person narrative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story type: first-person, narrative-driven account of travel experiences, emphasizing voice and scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend story — pattern across many places
rubrics_metrics.description: Trend story — pattern across many places
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story type: reporting that identifies and explains patterns affecting travel across multiple destinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile — person tied to place
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story type: a profile of an individual whose life/work illuminates aspects of a destination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adventure — extreme experience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story type: coverage of high-adrenaline or extreme experiences; often immersive with sensory detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food travel — culinary focus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story type: tourism framed around cuisine, chefs, markets, and food culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural critique — examines tourism's effects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story type: analytical pieces that interrogate the impacts of tourism on local communities and environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose sponsored trips / press trips
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics: transparently disclose sponsorships and press-trip arrangements to avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay for own meals when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay for own meals when possible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics: where feasible, pay for meals to avoid perceived or actual influence from complimentary hospitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid promoting unsustainable practices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics: do not glamorize or encourage tourism behaviours that harm environments or communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center local voices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics: elevate and prioritize perspectives of local people rather than speaking only as an outsider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping cultures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics: write respectfully and avoid reductive or exoticising portrayals of people and cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge colonial / extractive history
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics: situate tourism and place histories within broader contexts of colonialism and extraction where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative arc in story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit quality marker: even service pieces benefit from storytelling structure—a beginning, development, and resolution or insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory specificity (smells, sounds, textures)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit quality marker: use concrete sensory details to bring places to life for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local voice integration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit quality marker: incorporate the voices of local people to deepen authenticity and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-aware tourism critique
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit quality marker: be reflective about the ethics and impacts of tourism rather than uncritical promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical without being listicle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit quality marker: provide useful, actionable information while avoiding shallow list-style formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest about challenges of place
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit quality marker: candidly acknowledge difficulties, risks, or limitations travelers may encounter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic accompaniment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit quality marker: strong photography is often essential; plan for visuals that complement and enhance the text.
